description:
Turn ONE address into a point, with an honest account of how much of it was found. Built
for deliveries. South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Lesotho and Eswatini today;
more countries as their data loads. 1 lookup per address, found or not.

Send either q (one line) or address (housenumber, street, suburb, city, postcode, unit) —
never both. If the address is already split, send it split: it matches better.

READ precision BEFORE using the point. "address" means the house was found — or the plot
or stand, as Botswana and Zimbabwe write addresses ("Plot 1225, Kasane", "Stand Y116,
Harare"), with its number in matched.housenumber and no matched.street;
"interpolated" means it was estimated between the numbers either side; "intersection"
means a street corner ("Cnr Main Rd and Belmont Rd", "Bree & Strand Streets"), at the
point where the two meet, with the second street in matched.crossStreet; "site" means a
named site — a shopping centre, office park, complex or estate, hospital, school, airport
or hotel — at a point inside it, named in matched.site; "street" means the right street
but NOT the house; "locality" means only the suburb or town. NEVER present
a street- or locality-level point as a door: a driver sent there will be at the wrong
house. In South Africa most answers are street-level, because OpenStreetMap has house
numbers on about 13% of street names — that is the data being honest, not a failure.

What to do with an answer — the result line says which applies:
- address, interpolated, intersection or site, not ambiguous, confidence 0.5 or more:
  dispatch. For a site, pass on the unit or shop number from the original address
  ("Shop 12") — the answer does not include it, and the driver needs it.
- street: ask the recipient for a pin or a landmark.
- ambiguous, or locality: ask the customer before dispatching.
When the advice is to ask the customer, ASK — do not pick one. result.alternatives holds up
to 4 other candidates the answer was chosen from, and the result line lists them with the
suburb each lies in and its distance and direction from the first, because they often
share a street name AND a town (five "Long Street, Cape Town"s: City Centre, Observatory,
Maitland…). Put the first answer and those to the user, by suburb. Free: still one lookup.
matched.locality is the place the caller wrote; matched.suburb is the suburb the point
actually lies in, absent at locality precision and where no suburb is near.
confidence ranks answers; it is NOT a probability. ambiguous means a same-named street
elsewhere scored about as well, or the street was a near-miss spelling with no house
number to confirm it. result null means nothing trustworthy was found, and that still
costs the lookup.

Some addresses name something that cannot be placed: in South Africa an erf, stand, plot or
farm portion (land parcels — there is no cadastre); a plot or stand number elsewhere that
the data does not hold; a PO box or private bag anywhere. Those parts come back in
unmatched and the answer is the place named, at locality: ask the customer for a street
address.

country is a hard filter; region (ZA-WC, or "Western Cape") only ranks streets inside it
first, so a wrong province does not lose the address. OUTSIDE SOUTH AFRICA, PASS country
(NA, BW, ZW, LS, SZ): without it a same-named place in South Africa can win ("Kingsway,
Maseru" without LS answers a Kingsway in South Africa). An uncovered country is refused,
unbilled, with the list of covered countries in the message — that message is the live
coverage list; there is no other. sets and base answer "which delivery zone is it in" in
the same call, at no extra cost.

One address per call, deliberately. For a delivery list, call this once per row so the
user sees what is being spent; programs with thousands of rows should use the API’s
POST /geocode/batch directly. Not for: searching for a business or landmark by name,
or a coordinate to an address (that is lookup_location with the street layer).

address.description: The address already split into parts. Needs a street, or a plot or stand number in housenumber with city or suburb for the place. Use instead of q.

base.description: Administrative layers to resolve at the found point.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: ZA, NA, BW, ZW, LS or SZ today. A hard filter: only that country is searched. Pass it outside ZA.

q.description: The whole address on one line, e.g. "25 Adderley Street, Cape Town".

region.description: ISO 3166-2 ("ZA-WC") or a name ("Western Cape"). A preference, not a filter.

sets.description: Boundary sets on this account to match at the found point, e.g. delivery zones.

streetGeometry.description: The matched street’s line, trimmed to about 250 m. Only if something will draw it.
